judgments.rationale: The proposed edit imports the limitation from paragraph (5) (F010) into the summary of paragraph (1). Because paragraph (5) is already captured as an independent record in the draft (C0007), incorporating it here violates the instruction that another record retaining a condition does not incorporate it into this statement. The edit is therefore unnecessary.

The proposed edit contradicts the source text by converting a permissive exception applicable only when an individual requests an accompanying person ('the agency may require the individual to furnish a written statement authorizing discussion... in the accompanying person's presence') into a mandatory duty covering all individuals ('the agency must require every individual, whether accompanied or unaccompanied, to furnish written authorization before access'). It also improperly imports paragraph (5).

The existing draft reading for C0000 is complete, faithful, and independently usable. It accurately captures the agency actor, the mandatory obligation under subsection (d), the access rights and copy conditions under paragraph (1), and the agency's discretionary authority to require a written statement authorizing discussion in the accompanying person's presence. Leaving the reading unchanged is correct.

source_spans.quote: (d) Access to Records.— Each agency that maintains a system of rec­ords shall—

(1) upon request by any individual to gain access to his record or to any information pertaining to him which is contained in the system, permit him and upon his request, a person of his own choosing to accompany him, to review the record and have a copy made of all or any portion thereof in a form comprehensible to him, except that the agency may require the individual to furnish a written statement authorizing discussion of that individual’s record in the accompanying person’s presence;
(5) nothing in this section shall allow an individual access to any information compiled in reasonable anticipation of a civil action or proceeding.
